default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-698.title: Volume-fading run fade
E-698.hypothesis: A run of same-colour bars each on less volume than the one before is a push with no new participants; the other side absorbs it, so fade the run.

E-699.title: Day-open extension fade
E-699.hypothesis: Distance from the session open beyond what is typical for that minute of day marks a stretched move that liquidity providers fade back toward the open.

E-700.title: Squeeze false-release fade
E-700.hypothesis: After a volatility squeeze, a first close outside the band is often a stop-run; fade it back inside.

E-701.title: Lunch-hour VWAP stretch fade
E-701.hypothesis: In the thin midday session stretches away from VWAP lack follow-through and revert as institutions benchmark to VWAP.

E-702.title: Prior-close extension rollover
E-702.hypothesis: After a big extension from yesterday's close, a retrace of a large part of it shows the late participants are trapped; follow the move back toward the prior close.

E-703.title: EMA distance z-score fade
E-703.hypothesis: A price far from its EMA in units of its own recent deviation is statistically stretched; fade back to the mean.

E-704.title: Morning extreme afternoon poke rejection
E-704.hypothesis: The morning high/low is a level that resting orders defend; an afternoon poke beyond it that closes back inside is a failed breakout.

E-705.title: Effort without result break
E-705.hypothesis: Rising volume while price stays in a narrow range means a large player is working an order; the break of that range shows the direction of the size.

E-706.title: Same-minute spike fade
E-706.hypothesis: A one-bar return many times larger than typical for that minute is usually a thin-book overshoot; fade it.

E-707.title: Hourly VWAP stretch fade
E-707.hypothesis: Traders and algos benchmark by clock hour; a price stretched from the current hour's VWAP late in the hour reverts as the hour rolls.
